policy: Comparison identifies overlap, difference, evidence and limitations; it does not pre-assign superiority.

comparisons.overlap: impartiality and protection against arbitrary advantage
comparisons.difference: Nishpaksh proposal emphasizes heart-oriented self-realization and family-to-global ecological scope; Rawls provides a formal political theory of justice
comparisons.testable_next_step: define impartial decision rules and evaluate outcomes across affected groups

comparisons.overlap: viewing conduct from perspectives beyond one's own interests
comparisons.difference: Nishpaksh proposal seeks a more explicit continuous self-realization and systems-governance layer
comparisons.testable_next_step: construct multi-perspective decision protocol and adversarial cases

comparisons.overlap: open scrutiny and attention to perspectives of others
comparisons.difference: Nishpaksh proposal adds an explicit heart/inner-stability vocabulary and integrated nature-protection objective
comparisons.testable_next_step: compare decision quality under closed vs open perspective procedures

comparisons.difference: Nishpaksh proposal adds a philosophical objective of continuous satisfaction and impartial understanding
comparisons.testable_next_step: define measurable learning, equity, wellbeing and access outcomes

comparisons.overlap: human activities are major drivers of biodiversity and ecosystem change; need transformative responses
comparisons.difference: Nishpaksh proposal seeks to embed ecological protection into a broader governance architecture
comparisons.testable_next_step: map proposed governance controls to measurable biodiversity, pollution and resource indicators

comparisons.overlap: ecological, economic and social needs must be considered together
comparisons.difference: Nishpaksh proposal makes impartiality and human decision architecture a central organizing principle
comparisons.testable_next_step: pilot integrated decision model with independent ecological and social evaluation
